clue.text: Fundraising caper supported by party liberals — it could flop?

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported means sitting on top, so what follows goes underneath

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity stunt, as in rag week
a do is a party
L for liberal, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A charity stunt backed by a party's liberal wing looks likely to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ragdoll is a cat breed famous for going limp when picked up, and a rag doll is a floppy toy; it is one of the cats at 1, 20, 27A and 27D.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth toy with no stiffening, or the breed of cat that relaxes completely when held, will collapse limply.

clue.text: Small dot left in for first time

indicators.note: something coming in for the first occurrence of a letter takes its place there

parts.note: a tittle is the small dot over an i or j
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A tiny dot was left inside for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the first T of TITTLE with L to get LITTLE; 'time' is part of the indicator, not T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of slight size, a plain adjective synonym.

clue.text: Woodland entered by old track

indicators.note: a place entered by something has that thing go inside it

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A woodland crossed by an ancient path.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a channel or rut, and the spiral cut on a record is called its track.

clue.text: Poetic twilit periods, part of compline/vespers

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the slash between the two service names

explanation.surface: Evening church services, compline and vespers, are poetically twilight periods.
explanation.walkthrough: Compline and vespers are evening services in the church day, so the hiding place suits the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve is a literary word for evening, the time of twilight, so the plural fits these periods.

clue.text: Footballer — one with a drinking problem maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a player who runs with the ball at their feet

definitions.text: one with a drinking problem maybe
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who lets drink run down their chin

explanation.walkthrough: A 'drinking problem' suggests alcoholism, but here it is just messy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To dribble is both to move a ball with small kicks and to let liquid trickle from the mouth.

clue.text: Legacy broadcast via radio tower

indicators.note: something heard over the radio is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to broadcast a programme is to air it, and that word is pronounced like one who inherits
to loom is to tower over

explanation.surface: An inheritance transmitted through a radio mast.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a treasured possession passed down a family, a bequest from earlier generations.

clue.text: Beer brewed by the German producer and seller of 1, 20, 27A and 27D, for instance

definitions.text: producer and seller of 1, 20, 27A and 27D, for instance

indicators.note: brewing turns ingredients into something new, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Beer brewed by a German maker, oddly, is linked to some other clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are cat breeds: Ragdoll, Persian, Munchkin and Manx. Someone who raises such cats for sale is a breeder.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeder raises animals such as pedigree cats and sells the kittens.

clue.text: One's journey begins in the ranks?

definitions.text: One's journey begins in the ranks?

parts.words: One's journey begins in the ranks?
parts.note: surface reading: a soldier who started out as a private and rose up
setter's reading: the ranks are cab ranks, where a hire car waits before each fare

explanation.walkthrough: 'The ranks' suggests an army career; in fact it is a taxi rank, where each trip for this driver starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab driver picks up passengers at a rank, so each trip literally starts there.

clue.text: Lear composed 'Grey' for example

indicators.note: to compose is to put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Edward Lear wrote a poem called 'Grey'.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey was a British prime minister, now best known from the tea named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Grey, the second Earl Grey, was a nobleman of that title, so Grey is an example.

clue.text: Versions of equality, diversity and inclusion touted primarily by international statisticians

parts.note: EDI is the standard workplace abbreviation

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: its opening letter
I is the abbreviation for international
the ONS, Office for National Statistics, is the UK government statistics body

explanation.surface: Different takes on diversity policy being promoted by international number crunchers.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one version of a published work, such as a revised printing.

clue.text: Ban left-wing type of crossword

parts.note: to bar is to forbid
red is the colour of the political left

explanation.surface: Prohibiting a left-wing style of puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ban' looks like the definition; it is the first piece, and the definition is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A barred crossword uses thick bars between cells instead of black squares, a common format for advanced puzzles.

clue.text: Superlatively silky southern vegetable, best when tip discarded

indicators.note: discarding the tip means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a leek is a vegetable
taken as written, before the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A southern vegetable that is the silkiest of all, best eaten trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek means smooth and glossy, and 'superlatively' asks for the -est form of that adjective.

clue.text: Jeong perhaps appearing in Gene Kelly retrospective

indicators.note: looking back means the letters are read from right to left
the answer appears inside the following words as a run of letters

parts.note: the run straddles the two parts of the name

explanation.surface: An actor shows up in a film season celebrating Gene Kelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Jeong is an American comic actor, known from The Hangover and Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeong's first name is that word, so the surname stands as an example of a person so named.

clue.text: Spooner's rendition of Bad, or Golden Brown

indicators.note: Spooner swapped sounds between words, here the consonants inside a single word are exchanged

parts.note: bad as in naughty; swap the n and t sounds

explanation.surface: Two song titles: Michael Jackson's 'Bad' and the Stranglers' 'Golden Brown'.
explanation.walkthrough: Say NAUGHTY with its n and t sounds swapped and you get TAWNY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawny is a warm yellowish-brown, the colour of a lion or tawny owl.

clue.text: 2, 11, 14 or 28 perhaps, swapping husband for Latin raider

indicators.note: one letter is taken out and another put in its place

parts.note: those answers each precede 'owl' in a bird's name, and an owl hoots
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: Several other clues, with a husband changed for a Latin raider.
explanation.walkthrough: Little, barred, tawny and barn owls are species; an owl is a hooter. H (husband) gives way to L.
explanation.definitionFit: A looter plunders goods, as a raider does during a riot or attack.

clue.text: Disturbed if woman drew curtains in front of this?

indicators.note: disturbed things are moved out of place, so these letters get reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that a woman pulled the curtains across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew curtains' reads as one phrase, but 'drew' belongs to the anagram and 'curtains' to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains hang across the glazed opening and its surround, so they are in front of it.

clue.text: Among others, Portuguese and Russian cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a Siberian is a Russian from Siberia

explanation.surface: Portuguese and Russian riders out on bikes, among others.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the S of SIBERIAN from the front to the back to get IBERIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian peninsula holds Portugal and Spain, so Portuguese people are among its natives.

clue.text: Awkwardly snog nude in damp dark places?

indicators.note: done awkwardly means clumsily out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy naked kiss in gloomy, damp spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Snog is British slang for a passionate kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungeons are underground prison cells, typically cold, wet and unlit.

clue.text: Starts to appreciate silvery hair colour

indicators.note: starts are opening letters, so only the first of each word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Learning to like grey hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a pale silvery grey, as in ash-blond hair.

clue.text: Asian language according to Welsh woman?

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per the rules'
Sian is a common Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: Is this an Asian language, says a woman from Wales?
explanation.walkthrough: It is also a cat breed, one of the cross-references in 7 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Persian, or Farsi, is the main tongue of Iran in western Asia.

clue.text: Terribly ironic about introduction to satire that's biting

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round another
something done terribly is done badly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Very ironic satire with a sharp edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biting' looks like a description of the satire; it defines a cutting tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is a front tooth used for cutting food, the one that does the biting.

clue.text: Cut new flower

parts.note: to sever is to cut
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A freshly cut bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower here is something that flows, a river; the Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is often a river, since a river is something that flows.

clue.text: Cynthia's disastrous end to outing at sea?

definitions.text: Cynthia's disastrous end to outing at sea?

indicators.note: a disastrous outcome leaves things in a mess, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the name, taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is used

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: Cynthia's day out on the water ended in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a boating trip on the sea that ends badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing for pleasure in a sleek boat is a typical trip on the water, and it can go wrong.

clue.text: Frank, defiant response to "You can't do that!"?

definitions.text: defiant response to "You can't do that!"
definitions.note: two words, CAN DID, run together
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a retort that I can, and indeed I already have

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as CAN DID: 'I can, and I did!' is the defiant retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A candid person speaks openly and honestly, the same as being frank.

clue.text: I drained tequila shot first, somewhere in the South Pacific

indicators.note: first says what comes before the lone letter that opens the clue
a drained word has its insides emptied out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: its first and last letters
a shot that strikes is a hit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Downing a tequila shot on a tropical island holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia, in the southern Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Have ambition when ripe for revolution

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Political ambition when the time is right for an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's hopes on achieving something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Artist related to member of the Lollipop Guild?

parts.note: Edvard Munch was the Norwegian painter of The Scream
kin are relatives; 'related' as in 'kin to'

explanation.surface: A painter connected with a sweet-sounding guild.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lollipop Guild sing a song in The Wizard of Oz. It is also a short-legged cat breed, cross-referenced at 7 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: In the film of The Wizard of Oz, the little people of Munchkinland include the Lollipop Guild trio.

clue.text: From site of motorcycle races, some perform anxiously

indicators.note: some means a portion of the following words, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: Riders at a famous motorbike track perform nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT motorcycle races are held on the Isle of Man; Manx is also the tailless cat in 7 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Manx is the adjective for things belonging to the Isle of Man, home of the TT races.

clue.text: Bran mixture for bovine body building

indicators.note: a mixture stirs things together, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A bran-based feed for building up muscle in cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body building' suggests muscle; read it as a building for bovine bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a farm building where cows and other livestock are housed.

clue.text: Half-cut Bannon drunk tonic if telling the truth!

indicators.note: with half cut away, only one half of the name remains

parts.note: the surname, of which the second half is kept

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Steve Bannon, half drunk on tonic, is supposedly telling the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for tipsy, but here it means cut in half. Steve Bannon is a US political strategist.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonfiction writing deals with real facts and events, not invented stories.
